title: Lloyd Lambert's band as a family
summary: Cotton wishes he had recorded the band; he recalls Miller Sam, Gilbo, and the trumpeter Brian, and a memorable night at an armory.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You had done reel-to-reel and done some recordings yourself?

No I would have had a recording of the band when we played, various places man, because we had a, Lloyd had a hell of a band out there man, it was like family. We had some fine musicians, they always, when one leaves somebody else would replace that guy. And we had a guy named Miller Sam, he's originally from Louisiana but he's been living in Detroit for the last 30 or 40 years. And he was a hell of a saxophone player. And his cousin, Gilbo, who played with Ray Charles, he came down there and had a guy we met in Columbus, Ohio named Brian, he was a trumpet player. We played in Clifford Browns a long time, somewhere in Delaware.

We played at some armory over there man, and you should have heard that. My wife even talked about that night when those guys played from, I mean from the beginning of the set to the end of the set. It was just beautiful man.
It seems to me, is it true that there are a lot of guys from New Orleans who played in road bands that just used New Orleans as kind of home base and went out and they hardly played in New Orleans?
I can't think of everything man, I have to do it. A lot of stuff I've forgotten man.
